## Optional: Spark / Hadoop

MGTA 466 uses an optional Spark/Hadoop profile. `rsm-update` creates
`~/rsm-msba/mgta466` and seeds the three course notebooks plus
`Shakespeare.txt` into `mgta466/examples/test`. The first profile activation
downloads Spark and Hadoop, so expect a wait.

```bash
rsm-update
rsm-scalable check                 # Spark, HDFS, and the three bundled notebooks
rsm-scalable                       # enter the profile in ~/rsm-msba/mgta466
code examples/test                 # open the bundled exercises
```

The check uses temporary HDFS data and stops its services when done. In the
`rsm-scalable` shell, select **Python (Spark/Hadoop)** for the notebooks. For a
persistent interactive HDFS exercise, run:

```bash
rsm-hdfs init                      # safe to repeat; preserves existing data
rsm-hdfs start
rsm-hdfs status
rsm-hdfs urls                      # NameNode and DataNode pages
rsm-hdfs stop                      # when finished with the exercise
```

HDFS data lives in `~/rsm-msba/.rsm-msba/hdfs`. The final section of
`hdfs-handson-test.ipynb` calls `rsm-hdfs reset --yes` and erases that data;
skip it when you want to keep your files. On the shared MSBA server, run the
check from your own account, use only the supplied public exercise data, and
stop a persistent HDFS instance when finished. The bundled PySpark notebook
uses one local worker, and Hadoop JVMs have a 512 MB heap limit.
